question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the minimum value of the function $f(x,y,z)=xy+{z}^{2}$ on the intersection of the surfaces ${z}^{2}+{x}^{2}=4$ and $x+2y=-2$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨y,\,x,\,2z⟩=\lambda ⟨\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,0,\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,0⟩ \\ {z}^{2}+{x}^{2}=4 \\ x+2y=-2\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing expressions?
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the minimum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy+{z}^{2}
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)={z}^{2}+{x}^{2}=4,\,h(x,y,z)=x+2y=-2.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=4 \\ h(x,y,z)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨y,\,x,\,2z⟩ & =\lambda ⟨2x,\,0,\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
